tradition.title: What is a Daruma?
tradition.text: Daruma dolls are Japanese good luck charms, modeled after Bodhidharma, the founder of Zen. They are weighted at the bottom, so they always stand back up: fall down seven times, get up eight.
tradition.hint: Tip: tap the Daruma to make it wobble, or swipe sideways to turn it.

first_eye.title: One eye for your goal
first_eye.text: A Daruma comes without eyes. When you set yourself a goal, you paint in its left eye. From then on, the one-eyed Daruma reminds you of what you set out to do.

second_eye.title: The second eye for success
second_eye.text: Once you reach your goal, the Daruma gets its second eye as a thank you. In Japan, Darumas are brought back to the temple at the end of the year and burned in a ceremony.

first_daruma.title: Your first Daruma
first_daruma.text: What do you want to achieve? Choose a color, put your goal into words and paint the first eye.
